records.key: Economic profit becomes $12,000 because accounting profit rises while implicit cost falls
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: Initially implicit costs are $84,000. They fall to $78,000 while accounting profit rises to $90,000; economic profit is $12,000. These changes reinforce each other, rather than offsetting. Normal profit is the return required to cover the owner’s alternatives.

records.key: Today labor varies around a fixed kiln; at renewal both kiln capacity and labor can be chosen
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: The short run is defined by a fixed input, not a fixed number of months. Staffing can vary today around the existing kiln. At renewal the firm can change capacity as well as staffing; a future lease payment is not the same as an unrecoverable past payment.

records.key: $72,000 accounting profit; $8,000 economic profit
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: Explicit payments total $96,000, leaving accounting profit of $72,000. Forgone salary and rent total $64,000 in implicit costs, leaving $8,000 economic profit. Owning the workshop does not make its alternative rental use free.

records.key: The current lease is unavoidable; next year the larger plant costs $9,000 less in total
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: The current commitment does not disappear with shutdown. Next year total cost is $24,000 + $8 × 9,000 = $96,000 in the old plant and $42,000 + $5 × 9,000 = $87,000 in the larger one. Future capacity costs are avoidable choices. The larger plant saves $9,000 at this output, not at every output.

records.key: Use the compact plant at 4,000 and the automated plant at 8,000; the switch occurs at 6,000 units
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: Set the two total costs equal: $24,000 = $4Q, so the crossover is 6,000. At 4,000 units costs are $54,000 versus $62,000; at 8,000 they are $90,000 versus $82,000. Long-run planning selects the lower attainable cost at each output; this comparison does not infer diminishing marginal returns.

records.key: Entry shifts market supply right; price and each firm’s horizontal MR fall; firm output falls along rising MC until P = minimum ATC
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: At the displayed Q = 90, price is $40 and ATC is $20, so profit attracts entry. Entry adds market supply. The lower market price lowers each firm’s horizontal MR line; with fixed cost curves its best output falls along rising MC. Under the stated benchmark assumptions entry ends at zero economic profit, P = MC = minimum ATC.

records.key: Its horizontal MR line rises, it expands output along MC, and economic profit increases
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: Market demand raises the equilibrium price. The firm takes that price as P = MR, so the higher horizontal line intersects rising MC at more output. With unchanged costs and initial zero profit, it can earn positive short-run profit before entry responds.

records.key: Produce 30 units with a $300 loss; revenue covers variable cost
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: The horizontal $30 price line meets rising MC at Q = 30. ATC is $40 and AVC is $20 there. Profit is (30 - 40) × 30 = -$300, but price covers AVC, so operating limits the short-run loss.

records.key: Demand first raised price and firm output; profit induced entry; added supply lowered firm MR and output until zero profit returned with more firms
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: The demand shock raises price, MR and each incumbent’s output initially. Profit attracts new firms, shifting industry supply right. Unchanged input prices keep firm cost curves fixed, so price returns to minimum ATC and each firm returns to its original output. Higher final market output is supplied by more firms, with zero economic profit.

records.key: The firm operates because P exceeds AVC; persistent losses induce exit; market supply falls and survivors’ MR and output rise until losses disappear
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: The displayed price lies between AVC and ATC, so production covers variable cost and some unavoidable fixed cost. Persistent economic losses discourage renewal and induce exit. Reduced market supply raises price and each survivor’s horizontal MR; output rises along unchanged rising MC until the standard long-run zero-profit condition is restored.

records.key: Zero economic profit while covering all opportunity costs
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: The higher fixed cost raises ATC without moving the MR = MC output or demand price. When ATC reaches P1 at Q1, revenue covers all economic costs and economic profit becomes zero. The original plotted curves need not already show tangency.

records.key: 16 units, $52 price, $320 profit

records.key: The rule can expand mutually beneficial service, but public financing and weak cost-control incentives under automatic cost reimbursement must be assessed
records.review: Key follows the stated constraints; distractors violate the relevant cost, marginal, market or welfare comparison. No routing metadata changed.
records.feedback: Cost-covering P = ATC leaves price above MC, excluding some positive-surplus uses. Setting P = MC can recover those uses but, with ATC > MC, leaves a cost-recovery gap.
